info.title: Zoho Analytics API
info.description: API for managing users and groups in Zoho Analytics — covering org-level users, workspace-level users, and workspace groups.

tags.name: Org Users
tags.description:
APIs that allow the Account Admin and the Organization Admins of a Zoho Analytics organization to manage its users - listing, adding, removing, activating, deactivating and changing the org-level role of the users, and listing the users who hold the Organization Admin role.

These APIs operate at the organization level. They govern the membership and role of a user within the organization, and not their access to individual workspaces, which is handled by the workspace sharing APIs.

Zoho Analytics also supports Client Portal (White Label) deployments, where an organization can have one or more custom-branded portal domains. When the Account Admin of the organization is also a Client Portal Admin, the write APIs in this group can be scoped to a specific portal domain using the `domainName` field in CONFIG. Users belonging to a portal domain are managed independently of the main organization domain, and `domainName` must be a valid portal domain owned by the Account Admin of the organization.

tags.name: Custom Roles
tags.description:
APIs that allow the Account Admin and the Organization Admins of a Zoho Analytics organization to define custom roles - named permission bundles that can be granted to users in place of the built-in roles.

A custom role is organization-scoped and is made of three parts: a role name, an access type that decides which kinds of view the role can reach (dashboards only, reports and dashboards, or the underlying data as well), and a set of boolean permissions arranged in seven groups. The access type acts as a ceiling - enabling a permission that lies above the chosen access type is rejected with a specific error rather than being silently ignored.

These APIs define roles only. Attaching a role to a user or to a workspace is done through the user management and workspace sharing APIs. The custom roles feature must be enabled for the organization and included in its subscription plan, and none of these APIs is available through a Client Portal (White Label) custom domain.

tags.name: Workspace Users
tags.description:
APIs that manage the users and the administrators of a single Zoho Analytics workspace - controlling who has access to the workspace, the role they hold within it, and whether that access is currently active.

These APIs complement the org-level user management APIs. Org-level management controls who is a member of the organization at all, while workspace-level management controls which of those members can access a specific workspace and in what capacity.

When the Account Admin of the organization is also a Client Portal Admin, the operations in this group can be scoped to a specific portal domain using the `domainName` field in CONFIG. Users belonging to a portal domain are listed and managed separately from the standard Zoho Analytics users.

tags.name: Workspace Groups
tags.description:
APIs that manage the groups of a Zoho Analytics workspace. A group is a named collection of users within a single workspace.

Groups are the building block for bulk view-level access management. When a view is shared with a group, every current and future member of that group inherits that sharing - which makes group membership the way to batch-update the sharing permissions of several users at once. Adding a member grants them access to every view currently shared with the group, removing a member revokes that access unless they hold it through another path, and deleting a group revokes it for every member simultaneously.

Groups are scoped to a single workspace, and their members must already be users of that workspace. When the Account Admin of the organization is also a Client Portal Admin, a group can be scoped to a specific portal domain using the `domainName` field at creation. That association is fixed for the life of the group, and the member management APIs resolve the domain context from the group rather than taking it as an attribute.

get.description:
Returns the list of all the users who are members of the specified organization, along with their current status and org-level role.

The org-level role governs what the user can do across the entire organization. It is distinct from the workspace-level role, which governs what the user can do within a specific workspace and is managed using the workspace sharing APIs.

get.description:
Returns every custom role defined in the organization identified by the ZANALYTICS-ORGID header, along with the complete permission definition of each role.

This is the only way to read a role definition back - there is no get-by-ID variant. The accessType and permissions returned for a role are in exactly the shape accepted by the Update Custom Role API, so a role can be read, edited and posted back without any transformation.

noCustomRoles.summary: Organization in which no custom role has been defined yet. An empty array is a success, not an error.

1.value:
Note:
  • The calling user must be an Account Admin or Organization Admin of the organization. No other role qualifies - Workspace Admins, view owners, users holding a custom role and shared users all fail with error code 7301.
  • The custom roles feature must be enabled for the organization, otherwise the API fails with error code 7301 even for an Account Admin. A subscription plan that does not include custom roles fails with error code 6142.
  • This API is not available through a Client Portal (White Label) custom domain. Such requests are rejected with error code 7301 before any business logic runs.
  • There is no path parameter for the organization - the roles returned belong to the organization named in the ZANALYTICS-ORGID header.
  • This is the only API that reads a role definition. There is no get-by-ID variant, so filter the returned list client-side on roleId or roleName.
  • The response is always complete - all seven permission groups and every flag are returned, including the ones set to false. This differs from the request side of the Create and Update APIs, where an omitted flag is treated as false.
  • The accessType and permissions of a role are returned in exactly the shape accepted by the Update Custom Role API. Read the role here, change the flags needed and send the whole object back - this round-trip is the supported way to make a partial permission edit.
  • The roleId values returned here are required as the role-id path parameter of the Update Custom Role and Delete Custom Role APIs. They are returned as strings even though they are numeric.
  • The response reports role definitions only. It does not indicate which users hold a role.
  • The list is not paginated and its order is not guaranteed. Sort client-side if presentation order matters.

post.description:
Creates one custom role in the organization identified by the ZANALYTICS-ORGID header, and returns its identifier.

The role name, the access type and the permissions are all mandatory. The permissions are validated as a whole against the access type and against the cross-group dependency rules before anything is stored, so a rejected request creates nothing and can be corrected and retried safely.

dashboardOnlyRole.summary: Creates a role at the most restricted access level. No data, design or datasource permission may appear, and createFolder is the only creation flag available. export is enabled alongside manageEmailSchedules, as the dependency rule requires.

reportAnalystRole.summary: Creates a role that reaches reports as well as dashboards. Raising the access level unlocks manageDataAlerts, which ALL_DASHBOARDS would reject with error 7576.

fullAccessRole.summary: Creates a role at the only level that allows dataPermissions, designPermissions, datasourcePermissions and the table creation flags. designModify pulls in both preset permissions, useDatasource pulls in createTable, and every other datasource flag pulls in viewDatasource.

Note:
  • The calling user must be an Account Admin or Organization Admin of the organization, custom roles must be enabled for the organization, and the request must not arrive through a Client Portal (White Label) custom domain. Any of these failing yields error code 7301.
  • roleName, accessType and permissions are all mandatory. Omitting any of them fails with error code 8504; sending one with an empty value fails with error code 8539 or 8078.
  • roleName is limited to 1 to 30 characters made of letters, digits, spaces, underscore and hyphen, and must be unique across the organization - the uniqueness check covers built-in role names too. A longer name fails with error code 8507, disallowed characters fail with 8509, and a clash fails with 7553.
  • accessType is a ceiling. Every permission group is only available at or above a given level - see the CustomRolePermissions schema. Enabling a permission above the chosen level is an error (7573, 7574, 7575, 7576 or 7584 depending on the group), not a silent no-op.
  • interactionPermissions.read must be explicitly true. It is not defaulted - a permissions object that omits interactionPermissions entirely, or sets read to false, fails with error code 7579 before any other rule is evaluated.
  • Every flag that is omitted from permissions is treated as false. A group that is left out is entirely disabled.
  • Four rules reach across permission groups: designModify requires both accessAdminPresets and createPreset (7578); manageEmailSchedules requires export (7559); useDatasource requires createTable (7585); and editDatasource, syncData, useDatasource and removeDatasource each require viewDatasource (7586). dataArchives additionally requires every other data permission to be enabled (7577).
  • All validation runs before anything is stored, and the rules fire in a fixed order, so a payload with several problems reports one error at a time. A rejected request creates no role and is safe to correct and retry.
  • This API is not an upsert. Re-creating an existing name fails with error code 7553 rather than returning or updating the existing role.
  • One role is created per call. There is no bulk-create variant.
  • Creating a role grants nothing by itself. Until the role is assigned to a user or a workspace through the user management and sharing APIs, it has no effect.
  • Only the new roleId is returned. Use the Get Custom Roles API to read the stored definition back.

put.description:
Renames a custom role, replaces its access type and permissions, or does both in one call.

This is a replace, not a merge. Whenever permissions is supplied, the stored definition is discarded and rebuilt from the object sent - every flag left out becomes false. Read the current definition with the Get Custom Roles API, edit it, and send the whole object back. Sending roleName alone is the one edit that leaves the permission definition untouched.

replacePermissions.summary: Replaces the access level and the entire permission set after reading the current definition with the Get Custom Roles API. The role name is preserved. accessType is resent even though it is unchanged, because permissions cannot be sent on its own.

renameAndDowngrade.summary: Renames the role and lowers it to the dashboard-only level in one call. Every permission above the new ceiling has been removed from the payload - leaving a higher-level flag enabled would fail the request.

role.description:
Controls the workspace-level role assigned to the specified users.

- **WORKSPACEADMIN** - Workspace Admin. Has full access to the workspace and can add or remove users, create and delete views, and manage shares.
- **USER** - User. Can access the views shared with them, and cannot manage the workspace settings or its users unless they are specifically shared with the Design Modify permission.
- **Custom role name** - The exact name of a custom role defined in the organization. The name must match an existing custom role.

domainName.description: Custom domain name of the client portal in whose context the role change of this group has to be performed. When this is not provided, the action is performed in the standard Zoho Analytics domain context.

CustomRolePermissionsResponse.description: Complete permission definition of a custom role, in seven groups. Every group and every flag is always present in the response, including the ones set to false.

createFolder.description: Allows creating folders. Available at every accessType.

createTable.description: Allows creating tables and importing data into new ones. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7575.

createQueryTable.description: Allows creating query tables. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7575.

createFormula.description: Allows creating formula columns. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7575.

CreateCustomRoleConfig.title: CreateCustomRoleConfig
CreateCustomRoleConfig.description: Configuration that defines the custom role to be created. All three attributes are mandatory, and the permissions are validated as a whole against the access type before anything is stored.

roleName.description: Display name of the role. 1 to 30 characters made of letters, digits, spaces, underscore and hyphen only, and unique across the organization including against built-in role names - a clash fails with error 7553.

accessType.description: Access level of the role. It sets a ceiling on the permissions that may be enabled - see CustomRolePermissions. Each level includes everything below it.
x-zenesis-enums-desc: Dashboards only - the most restricted level
Reports and dashboards - additionally allows managing data alerts
Tables, reports and dashboards - the only level at which data, design, table creation and datasource permissions are available

UpdateCustomRoleConfig.title: UpdateCustomRoleConfig
UpdateCustomRoleConfig.description: Configuration that carries the changes to apply to an existing custom role. At least one of roleName or accessType must be present (otherwise error 7581), and accessType and permissions must always be sent together (otherwise error 7580). This leaves exactly three valid shapes: roleName alone, accessType with permissions, or all three.

roleName.description: New display name of the role. 1 to 30 characters made of letters, digits, spaces, underscore and hyphen only, and unique across the organization - a clash fails with error 7553. Omit to keep the current name. Sending roleName alone renames the role and leaves accessType and permissions untouched.

accessType.description: New access level of the role. Must be sent together with permissions, otherwise error 7580. Resend the current level if only the permissions change. Lowering the level requires every permission above the new ceiling to be absent or false in the same payload.
x-zenesis-enums-desc: Dashboards only - the most restricted level
Reports and dashboards - additionally allows managing data alerts
Tables, reports and dashboards - the only level at which data, design, table creation and datasource permissions are available

CustomRolePermissions.title: CustomRolePermissions
CustomRolePermissions.description: Permission definition of a custom role, in up to seven groups of boolean flags. Every flag that is omitted is treated as false, and a group that is left out is entirely disabled - which is why an update must resend the complete object. interactionPermissions.read must always be true (error 7579). The accessType of the role sets a ceiling: interactionPermissions, sharePermissions, createPermissions.createFolder and every publishPermissions flag except manageDataAlerts are available at every level; manageDataAlerts and allDataAlertsAccess need ALL_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS or higher; dataPermissions, designPermissions, datasourcePermissions and the remaining createPermissions need ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS. The serialized object is limited to 5,000 characters, and each group to 500.

CustomRoleCreatePermissions.title: CustomRoleCreatePermissions
CustomRoleCreatePermissions.description: Permissions related to creating folders, tables, query tables and formula columns. createFolder is available at every accessType; the other three require ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS. An omitted flag is treated as false.

createFolder.description: Allows creating folders. Available at every accessType.

createTable.description: Allows creating tables and importing data into new ones. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7575.

createQueryTable.description: Allows creating query tables. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7575.

createFormula.description: Allows creating formula columns. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7575.

CustomRoleDataPermissions.title: CustomRoleDataPermissions
CustomRoleDataPermissions.description: Permissions related to adding, changing and importing rows. Every flag in this group requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7573. An omitted flag is treated as false.

addRow.description: Allows adding rows to a table.

deleteRow.description: Allows deleting rows. Also confers the bulk delete-all-rows capability.

importAppend.description: Allows importing data in append mode.

importAddOrUpdate.description: Allows importing data in add-or-update mode.

importDeleteAllAdd.description: Allows importing data in delete-all-and-add mode.

importDeleteUpdateAdd.description: Allows importing data in delete-update-and-add mode.

dataArchives.description: Allows managing scheduled data deletion. Requires every other flag in this group to be true as well, otherwise error 7577.

CustomRoleDesignPermissions.title: CustomRoleDesignPermissions
CustomRoleDesignPermissions.description: Permissions related to changing the design of a view. Requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7574. An omitted flag is treated as false.

designModify.description: Allows changing the design of a view - formatting, layout and structure. Additionally requires sharePermissions.accessAdminPresets and sharePermissions.createPreset to be true, otherwise error 7578.

CustomRoleInteractionPermissions.title: CustomRoleInteractionPermissions
CustomRoleInteractionPermissions.description: Permissions related to viewing and exploring a view. Available at every accessType. An omitted flag is treated as false, except that read is mandatory.

read.description: Allows viewing the shared item. Must always be true - a missing or false value fails with error 7579 before any other rule is evaluated.

vud.description: Allows viewing the underlying data of a report.

drillDown.description: Allows drilling down within a report.

drillThrough.description: Allows drilling through to a linked report.

insight.description: Allows using the AI and insight features on a view.

CustomRoleSharePermissions.title: CustomRoleSharePermissions
CustomRoleSharePermissions.description: Permissions related to re-sharing, discussions, private links and presets. Available at every accessType. An omitted flag is treated as false.

share.description: Allows re-sharing a view with other users.

discussion.description: Allows taking part in view discussions and comments.

privateLinks.description: Allows generating private links for a view.

accessAdminPresets.description: Allows viewing presets created by the workspace administrator. Required, together with createPreset, when designModify is enabled.

createPreset.description: Allows creating personal filter and column presets. Required, together with accessAdminPresets, when designModify is enabled.

CustomRolePublishPermissions.title: CustomRolePublishPermissions
CustomRolePublishPermissions.description: Permissions related to exporting, email schedules, data alerts, slideshows and public views. Every flag except manageDataAlerts and allDataAlertsAccess is available at every accessType; those two need ALL_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS or higher, otherwise error 7576. An omitted flag is treated as false.

export.description: Allows exporting view data. Required when manageEmailSchedules is enabled.

manageEmailSchedules.description: Allows creating and editing email schedules. Requires export to be true, otherwise error 7559.

allEmailSchedulesAccess.description: Widens manageEmailSchedules from the schedules the user created to every email schedule. Has no effect unless manageEmailSchedules is true.

manageDataAlerts.description: Allows creating and editing data alerts. Requires accessType ALL_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS or higher, otherwise error 7576.

allDataAlertsAccess.description: Widens manageDataAlerts from the alerts the user created to every data alert. Has no effect unless manageDataAlerts is true. Requires accessType ALL_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS or higher.

publicViews.description: Allows making a view publicly accessible.

CustomRoleDatasourcePermissions.title: CustomRoleDatasourcePermissions
CustomRoleDatasourcePermissions.description: Permissions related to viewing and managing the datasource behind a table. Every flag in this group requires accessType ALL_DATA_REPORTS_AND_DASHBOARDS, otherwise error 7584. An omitted flag is treated as false.

viewDatasource.description: Allows seeing the datasource behind a table. Required by every other flag in this group, otherwise error 7586.

editDatasource.description: Allows changing datasource connection details. Requires viewDatasource.

syncData.description: Allows triggering a data sync. Requires viewDatasource.

useDatasource.description: Allows building new tables from an existing datasource. Requires viewDatasource and createPermissions.createTable, otherwise error 7585.

removeDatasource.description: Allows removing a datasource. Requires viewDatasource.

CreateGroupConfig.title: CreateGroupConfig
CreateGroupConfig.description: Configuration that controls the group to be created in the workspace and the initial members to be added to it.

groupName.description: Display name for the new group. It must be unique within the workspace, and an empty or blank value is rejected.

groupDesc.description: Description of the group. It can hold a maximum of 200 characters. When this is not provided, it defaults to an empty string.

domainName.description: Custom domain name of the client portal that the group has to be scoped to. Every email address in `emailIds` must belong to a user within that portal domain. When this is not provided, the group is created in the standard Zoho Analytics domain context.

inviteMail.description: Controls whether an invitation email has to be sent to all the initial members of the group informing them of their group access.

mailSubject.description: Custom subject line for the invitation email. Applicable only when `inviteMail` is set to true. It can hold a maximum of 500 characters. When this is not provided, a system generated subject is used.
examples: You've been added to the Analytics Team group

mailMessage.description: Custom message body for the invitation email. Basic HTML is supported. Applicable only when `inviteMail` is set to true. It can hold a maximum of 5000 characters. When this is not provided, a system generated message is used.
examples:
Hi,
You now have access to the Analytics workspace group.

GroupMemberEmailIds.title: GroupMemberEmailIds
GroupMemberEmailIds.description: JSONArray holding the email addresses of the users on whom the action has to be performed. A minimum of 1 and a maximum of 1000 email addresses can be sent in a single request. The users must already be members of the workspace, within the domain context that the group belongs to.

CreateGroupResponse.description: Response returned by the Create Group API. Only the identifier of the new group is returned - use the Get Group Details API to retrieve the full group record.

RenameGroupConfig.description: Configuration that controls the new name and description of the group. Both values are replaced atomically.

groupDesc.description: Description of the group. It can hold a maximum of 200 characters. When this is not provided, the existing description of the group is overwritten with an empty string - the previous value is not preserved.

GroupMembersConfig.title: GroupMembersConfig
GroupMembersConfig.description: Configuration that controls the users to be added to the group.

inviteMail.description: Controls whether an invitation email has to be sent to the newly added members informing them of their group access. Members who were already part of the group receive no email.

mailSubject.description: Custom subject line for the invitation email. Applicable only when `inviteMail` is set to true. It can hold a maximum of 500 characters. When this is not provided, a system generated subject is used.
examples: You've been added to the Analytics Team group

mailMessage.description: Custom message body for the invitation email. Basic HTML is supported. Applicable only when `inviteMail` is set to true. It can hold a maximum of 5000 characters. When this is not provided, a system generated message is used.
examples:
Hi,
You now have access to the Analytics workspace group.
